headline: Start counting only at the beginning of a run
statement: Given an unsorted array of integers, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integer values. Values do not need to be adjacent in the input, and duplicate values do not lengthen a sequence. Achieve expected O(n) time.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Put the values in a set so you can quickly check whether a number exists. Begin counting a consecutive run only at a value whose previous number is absent. This avoids counting the same long run again from every point inside it.
approach: Put nums in a set to remove duplicates.
For every value without a predecessor, walk through value+1, value+2, and so on.
correctness: Each maximal consecutive run has exactly one value without a predecessor. Its walk visits all and only that run. Every set value belongs to one such run, so all runs are measured and the maximum is correct. Duplicate removal matches the sequence definition.
bruteForce: Sort and scan distinct neighboring values in O(n log n) time. It is reliable but misses the required expected linear bound.

complexity.explanation: Each unique value is tested as a start and walked at most once across all runs. Hash-set storage is linear.

pitfalls: Iterate over the set, not nums, to avoid repeating long walks for duplicate starts.
Sequence means consecutive values, not contiguous input positions.
The empty input has length zero.
